newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF to cut deposit rate to 2.7 pct from April 9.
newsitem.headline: MOF to cut deposit rate to 2.7 pct from April 9.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Thursday it will cut the interest rate it pays to other ministries for their long-term deposits by 0.1 percentage point to 2.7 percent, effective from April 9.

The rate of 2.7 percent would be a record low and follow a fall in the coupon rate of the last auctioned 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB), on which the deposit rate is customarily set, a MOF official said.
The coupon rate fell to a record low of 2.5 percent for the 10-year JGB to be issued in April from 2.6 percent for the March issue.
"It didn't take as long as the last time (the rate was cut) because the ministries concerned were able to reach an agreement smoothly this time," the MOF official said.

The MOF's Trust Fund Bureau channels funds raised via deposits made by the Health Ministry and the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry to government-affiliated financial institutions and other quasi-governmental bodies for the fiscal investment and loan programme (FILP).
The timing of the last rate cut was delayed about a month because Health and Welfare Minister Junichiro Koizumi, a fierce opponent of the FILP, refused to accept the rate cut.
